text:
marco: Heads up — onboarding ranker-lite-int8 showed MRR +2.4% but NDCG@5 -3.7% on eval_small. suspicious pattern: head improves, tail tanks. anyone seen this pattern before? :wave:

selena: quick checklist: candidate ordering, score calibration, or a change in feature masking. did quant pipeline change any float->int clip?

marco: quant pipeline added a tiny post-scale clip: `clip_range=0.985`. not sure why but it was to avoid overflow on some kernels.

raj: interesting. clipping can compress score distribution which might raise top1 by moving a few close winners up but hurts graded metrics like ndcg. do you have histograms of scores (fp16 vs int8)?

marco: attaching small snippet inline:
```
score_hist_fp16 = [ -3.1, -1.7, -0.4, 0.2, 0.9 ]  # center quantiles
score_hist_int8 = [ -2.9, -1.2, -0.1, 0.15, 0.5 ]
mean_fp16= -0.64, mean_int8= -0.29
```
marco: looks like tail squeezed up toward head, mean shifted higher.

selena: that definitely smells like clipping causing lower dynamic range on negative scores. did we also change the softmax temperature or score scaling before softmax?

marco: nope, temperature same. but I also noticed the harness that builds candidate lists now dedups by url earlier in the pipeline (a change in preproc). could dedupe bias top vs tail?

olivia: dedupe tends to remove near-duplicate low-relevance docs (often duplicates of promoted content), that could hurt tail if those duplicates were contributing some graded relevance signal. but usually dedupe increases ndcg, not decreases.

raj: let's isolate: 1) run eval with clip_range disabled on int8 build, 2) run with original fp16 preproc but int8 model, 3) compare per-query top5 doc id lists. 

marco: kicked off three quick jobs: job-901 (int8, clip off), job-902 (int8, fp16 preproc), job-903 (int8 with per-query diffs enabled).

ci-bot: job-901 started (eval_small, shard=1).

ci-bot: job-902 started (eval_small, shard=1).

ci-bot: job-903 started (eval_small, shard=1).

(20m later)

ci-bot: job-901 finished. artifacts: s3://ci/901/metrics.json

olivia: job-901 (clip disabled) metrics:
```
MRR@10: 0.265 -> 0.271 (+2.3%)
NDCG@5: 0.403 -> 0.389 (-3.4%)
Top1: 0.548 -> 0.565
Tail avg (4-5): 0.142 -> 0.110
```

marco: clip off helped a bit on head but ndcg still down. job-902?

ci-bot: job-902 finished. artifacts: s3://ci/902/metrics.json

selena: job-902 (fp16 preproc) metrics:
```
MRR@10: 0.265 -> 0.270 (+1.9%)
NDCG@5: 0.403 -> 0.395 (-2.0%)
Top1: 0.548 -> 0.560
Tail avg (4-5): 0.142 -> 0.126
```

raj: so preproc dedupe mattered — restores some tail. clip also matters but neither alone recovers ndcg fully. job-903 diff logs?

ci-bot: job-903 finished. artifacts: s3://ci/903/diffs.json

olivia: per-query diffs show many queries where top1 changed from a mid-relevance doc to a very short snippet doc after quantization. those queries have small doc-lengths, and ranker-lite-int8 seems to prefer shorter snippets post-quant.

marco: aha. is there a length-bias introduced by quant kernels? maybe some features (like length embedding) quantized poorly.

selena: check feature buckets serialization — we recently moved length into a separate float feature vector that goes through a different quant path. could be rounding bias.

raj: action plan: 1) revert length serialization change for the int8 path, 2) remove clip or make it adaptive, 3) add per-query head/tail split to CI eval dashboard so we catch this earlier. Also add a small synthetic test that ensures short-long doc rank parity between fp16 and quant.

marco: I'll open PR #2487 with length serialization revert and an adaptive clip parameter (disabled by default). also adding a small unit test and a dashboard chart.

olivia: quick note for onboarding docs: include a short troubleshooting table for head-up vs tail-down patterns and likely culprits (ordering, clipping, feature quantization, preproc). saves time for future bringups.

marco: thanks — will add that to `onboarding/notes.md`.

selena: nice triage everyone. learning: aggregated metrics can hide directional shifts; always break metrics into head/tail and inspect top-k doc ids. :nerd_face:

ci-bot: artifacts uploaded for all jobs. repos: s3://ci/901/, s3://ci/902/, s3://ci/903/

marco: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/rerank/pull/2487 — assigning to @selena for review.

raj: bumping for review. I'll run a small canary after the revert to confirm parity.

olivia: thumbs up.

marco: closing thread — followups in the PR and canary tickets. thanks!
